title: Emrys and the Hollow
premise: Rosalind Dunmore has spent a decade hiding in plain sight as a charm-seller in Corvale, a city where magic is outlawed and his true work—keeping the Hollow Gate sealed—is a crime punishable by unmaking. When the border wards collapse and the stars vanish, the country's rulers blame sorcery and begin hunting anyone with the gift, forcing Rosalind to gather a ragtag found family: a disgraced wardens' apprentice, a smuggler who once loved him, and a child who can hear the Hollow breathing. As they cross a land being erased from maps and memory, Rosalind learns the Gate was never a prison but a wound, and that sealing it ten years ago cost him everything he loved. In the end he must choose between restoring the law that outlawed him and opening the door to whatever waits beyond, sacrificing his own name so that his found family—and a remade country—can exist at all.
about_author: Silas Voss is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing confiscated grimoires before turning to fiction. They write from a coastal town where the fog rolls in on schedule and the lighthouse keeper swears the stars blink back.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller's Hours
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. A quiet night in his charm shop establishes his double life: harmless trinkets by day, secret maintenance of the Hollow Gate by night. He refuses a desperate customer's plea for real magic, and guilt follows him home. Emotional beat: the loneliness of chosen invisibility.

chapters.title: Wards Like Broken Teeth
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. During his midnight rounds, the border wards shatter one by one, and the stars go out overhead like snuffed candles. He reaches the Hollow Gate and finds it humming, awake, hungry. Emotional beat: dread—the decade of hiding is over.

chapters.title: The Warden's Apprentice
chapters.summary: Ivet's POV. Ivet Kess, apprentice to the Wardens who enforce the magic ban, watches her mentor burn a neighbor's spellbooks and realizes the purge has begun. She flees with a stolen ledger listing every registered mage—including Rosalind Dunmore. Emotional beat: disillusionment curdling into defiance.

chapters.title: A Country Being Erased
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Official criers announce that the border towns 'no longer exist'; roads lead to fields that were never villages. Rosalind understands the Hollow is eating memory itself. Ivet arrives at his shop with the ledger and an ultimatum. Emotional beat: the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: What the Smuggler Kept
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram Ferrow, river smuggler and Rosalind's former lover, agrees to move them downstream—but only after a bitter reckoning over why Rosalind vanished ten years ago. The boat carries them past drowned lanterns burning under black water. Emotional beat: old love, still raw, still load-bearing.

chapters.title: The Child Who Hears It
chapters.summary: Ivet's POV. In a refugee camp they find Pip, an orphan who hums the Hollow's song without knowing it. Soldiers arrive to 'relocate' gifted children; the trio escapes with Pip through the reeds. Emotional beat: found family taking its first fragile shape.

chapters.title: Ledger of the Condemned
chapters.summary: Ivet's POV. Reading her stolen ledger, Ivet discovers the Wardens knew about the Gate all along and have been feeding it names to keep it quiet. Her loyalty to the order dies for good. Emotional beat: justice outside the law becomes personal.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Grave
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Seeking a mapmaker rumored to chart places that no longer exist, they find only his grave—and his daughter, Odile, who finishes her father's charts from memory. She reveals the Hollow's center lies beyond the capital. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Stars in a Bottle
chapters.summary: Pip's POV (close third). Pip catches a fallen star-fragment in a jam jar; inside it, everyone glimpses the world as it was before the erasure. Rosalind sees his own face among those who first sealed the Gate. Emotional beat: wonder shadowed by terrible recognition.

chapters.title: The Confession at Grayford Bridge
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Cornered by Wardens, Rosalind confesses to the group: ten years ago he helped seal the Gate, and the price was the erasure of his home village and everyone in it—including someone Bram loved. Bram walks into the dark alone. Emotional beat: love against duty, duty having won too long ago.

chapters.title: Interrogation of Ashes
chapters.summary: Ivet's POV. Captured and brought before High Warden Solmere, Ivet learns the purge isn't panic—it's harvest. Solmere intends to feed the city's mages to the Hollow and rule what remains. She escapes using the very magic she once enforced against. Emotional beat: betrayal by institutions, faith in people instead.

chapters.title: The Market of Unmade Things
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. In a black market trading goods salvaged from erased places—a doorknob from Rosalind's village, a wedding ring—Bram cools his anger and finds proof Rosalind's sacrifice saved thousands. He buys the doorknob. Emotional beat: forgiveness beginning as an act of will.

chapters.title: Reunion in the Flooded Chapel
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Ivet returns with news of Solmere's plan; Bram returns with the doorknob and no apology needed. The group vows to reach the Gate's heart before the next new moon, when Solmere's harvest will open it fully. Emotional beat: reconciliation, quiet and hard-won.

chapters.title: Odile's Map of Nowhere
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile completes the impossible map: the road to the Hollow's heart runs through terrain that exists only if you remember it aloud. The company travels by telling stories of lost places, each tale briefly rebuilding a bridge or field beneath their feet. Emotional beat: memory as resistance.

chapters.title: Solmere's Procession
chapters.summary: Ivet's POV. The company witnesses Solmere's column of chained mages winding toward the capital, meant for the harvest. Pip's humming grows frantic—the Hollow is excited. Against sense, they decide to strike the column rather than slip past. Emotional beat: justice demanding its price.

chapters.title: The Night of Small Rebellions
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The rescue: smugglers' tricks, Ivet's warden training, and ordinary citizens joining when they see the chained mages. Half are freed; Odile is gravely wounded holding a bridge of remembered stone. Emotional beat: courage contagious, cost undeniable.

chapters.title: What Pip Chose to Forget
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. To save Odile, Pip gives the star-fragment's memory-light freely—and in doing so glimpses the Hollow's heart: not a monster, but a grieving thing, the accumulated sorrow of everything erased. Pip stops fearing it. Emotional beat: compassion for the wound itself.

chapters.title: The Gate That Should Stay Shut
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. At the Hollow's threshold, Rosalind faces the truth he fled: the Gate cannot be sealed again, only answered. Beyond it waits everything the country discarded, including the erased dead, including his own erased self. Emotional beat: terror and longing braided together.

chapters.title: Harvest Moon
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. Solmere arrives with his army to force the Gate and claim its power; battle erupts on the threshold as the new moon rises. Ivet duels her former master; Bram holds the line; Odile's map keeps the battlefield from dissolving. Emotional beat: everything staked at once.

chapters.title: The Door Out of a Country That No Longer Exists
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Rosalind opens the Gate—not as a prison breached but as a door answered—and steps through to speak with the Hollow directly, offering it what it truly wants: to be witnessed, mourned, and released. Solmere, refusing witness, is taken by the erasure he wielded. Emotional beat: the climax as an act of love, not force.

chapters.title: Dawn With Stars In It
chapters.summary: Ivet's POV. The stars return; erased places resurface like divers coming up for air. Rosalind does not return whole—he gave his name to the Hollow as part of the bargain—but he comes back, known now only by the family who chooses to call him theirs anyway. Emotional beat: grief and grace in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Keeper of an Open Door
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV, epilogue. A year later, the shop reopens selling honest charms; the Gate stands as a tended doorway rather than a wound, with Rosalind, Ivet, Bram, Pip, and Odile keeping it together. Magic is debated openly in a country learning to trust itself. Final beat: love, freely chosen, outlasting both duty and law.
